item.title: Ralliston's Journey through all of the 001 proposals - Part Seven - Roget's Proposal II
item.content:encoded:
Review: This one frustrates me a lot. I found myself skimming through the description and the interviews a lot since most of it suffers from mistaking 'sounding smart and using big words' with 'being interesting'. Both of the parts of the article I mentioned could really be rewritten without sounding confusing and professional just for the sake of such.

All that being said however, the conclusion part and the ending gave me chills. They are absolutely phenomenal, and if the whole article would be like this, I wouldn't even dare to complain. I love the core idea this has, but it just tried too hard to make it sound smart and in the process sacrificed the great idea it has. I want to like this, I really do, but all of the smart-talk just kills all of the enthusiasm I had for it.

Result: A very sad no-vote

item.title: Not My Favourite
item.content:encoded:
Not feeling this one, if I'm being honest. I've read it over twice now and with exception of the excellent last section, which has some amazing atmosphere, I don't really vibe with it (For lack of a better term.) There were ~20 sentences where I had to read it multiple times to understand what you were trying to say. I get trying to make intentionally incoherent works but if your readers aren't sure what's a typo and what isn't, IMO you've made some creative mistakes.

It also felt really bloated in some parts, especially the interviews. I feel most of them, especially the Castro and Umbrella Man ones, didn't add anything to the story. Concepts were kind of just being thrown around left and right throughout that were never explored.

The bit under the footnotes was admittedly epic, but that doesn't save the article from more or less being weird and incoherent in a not so flattering way.

That'll be a downvote from me, sorry man.
